title: What is known about 1RB0LE_0RC0RA_1RD1RF_1LA0LD_1LD0RF_1RB---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LE_0RC0RA_1RD1RF_1LA0LD_1LD0RF_1RB---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Lean proves the sweeps, the ticks of the two common families for chains of any length and blocks of any size, one rebuild for every length of its last block, and that every halt must come from B>0 1 1 (kernel). It also proves no halt in the first 107 steps (native_decide). A C program checks the block form at all 30,932 right-end turns of the first 1010 steps.

What it does. The tape is 1010… cut into blocks (10)n by single extra cells, the separators (1 or 0). A round trip from the right end, a tick, sweeps left over some separators, turns at one, and sweeps back, complementing everything it crosses. Which separator it turns at, and how the block lengths change, depends on the separators and the parities of the blocks; two families of rules cover 30,528 of the 30,932 ticks of the first 1010 steps. The last block grows by one or two each tick, so the right edge grows smoothly.

The rebuilds. 238 of those ticks reach the left end instead. There the head works for a long time and rebuilds the front of the list; the same sequences of lists then recur with more blocks on the right, on larger and larger scales.

Where a halt would come from. Only F reading a 1 halts. Two steps before a halt the machine must be at B>0 1 1 (halt_route): E is entered only from A reading a 1, which leaves a 0 to E's right, so E>1 1 never occurs. In block terms B would have to stand on the last 0 of a block followed by a separator 1; in the run F always reads a 0.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 76,681 cells have been visited and 38,337 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: sqrt/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.389). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.554).

claims.title: Every way to a halt
claims.text: Two steps before any halt the machine is at B>0 1 1. In particular E>1 1, which would halt (halt_E), is never reached.

claims.title: The sweeps
claims.text: Moving left, A crosses 1010 in four steps and complements it; moving right, B crosses 10 in two steps and writes 01. Both for any number of copies.

claims.title: Two whole ticks
claims.text: From the right-end turn back to the next one: x | e becomes x . e+2 for every even e (8k+8 steps for e = 2k), and x | o | o' becomes x . o+1 | o'+1 for all odd o, o' ≥ 3 (written in the block notation: lengths of (10)-blocks, | a separator 1, . a 0).

claims.title: Tick chains of any length
claims.text: The two tick families, for chains of any length and blocks of any size: x | a . b1 . c1 . … . bk . ck . d . e with all blocks even (tick_chain) and x | p | a . b1 . c1 . … . d . e with p, a odd and the rest even (tick_chain_oo), from one right-end turn to the next, for every list of pairs, every size and every tape x. With tick_last and tick_oo (no pairs) this covers the families x | e (. e . e)k and x | o | o (. e . e)k for every k. The proof splits a tick into five pieces: entering, one pair on the way left, the turn, one pair on the way right, and leaving. Each piece is a symbolic run with unknown tape around it, and the passes over the pairs are inductions on the list.

claims.title: One rebuild, for every last block
claims.text: The left-end tick at step 22,986, 3|3|12|15|1.48.94 to 88|6|2|13|21|94, holds with the last block of any even length 2v+4 (8v + 16,500 steps). The rebuild reads the block 48 cell by cell, so that block cannot be made a variable this way.

claims.title: A first run 4 cells longer changes nothing else, for every way of entering it
claims.text: In the table of 32883 the head can step onto the last cell of the first run of the tape in five states, on a 0 or a 1. For each of these ten entries the outcome for a run of n + 4 cells is the outcome for n cells with one more copy of a 4-cell word: same exit state, same cells left behind. Proved for every bounce with any tape further left, and for every sweep with n = 4a + 5 to 4a + 8, all a. It holds for the three sister machines after renaming the states (and mirroring).

claims.title: The block form
claims.text: At every right-end turn of the first 1010 steps (30,932 turns) the tape is (10)n0 s1 (10)n1 … sk (10)nk A>1 1 with single separators si; the program stops if not.

claims.title: The tick rules
claims.text: Each tick of the first 1010 steps, run symbolically with the last block lengths as variables, follows a rule valid for all lengths of the same parities: 30,528 ticks are in the families x | e (. e . e)k and x | o | o (. e . e)k (the separator 1 becomes 0, the 0s after it become 1s, the blocks after it change by +1, −1, …, +1, +1), 30,674 follow one of 61 patterns, 238 reach the left end and 20 have a block of length 1 that the templates do not cover.

claims.title: Recurrence on growing scales
claims.text: The rebuild at step 22,986 (3|3|12|15|1.48.94 to 88|6|2|13|21|94) recurs at step 778,692 with three blocks more on the right (…1.48.212.258.468 to 88|6|2|13|21|210|259|469), and likewise 81,286 / 1,452,208; the list has 8 blocks at 106 steps, 12 at 109, 14 at 1010.

claims.title: Size of the tape description (family screen)
claims.text: At the 8 records between 2.6·10<sup>8</sup> and 1.7·10<sup>10</sup> steps (first new leftmost or rightmost cell after each threshold 10<sup>6</sup>·4^k) the tape has 39,174 to 337,957 visited cells and compresses to 20 to 27 level-2 tokens (repeats of a word of at most 40 cells, then repeats of groups of such tokens).

claims.title: Four machines, one run shifted (checked to 2·10<sup>12</sup> steps)
claims.text: The holdouts 32883, 40600, 103746 and 131976 are one table started in four states. Compared at the starts of their trips, the four runs from blank tape have the same list of run lengths except for the first run, which differs by a constant (r, r + 4, r + 8, r + 12), at every one of the first 527,004 trips, up to 2·10<sup>12</sup> steps. This is a computation; it does not show that the four halt together.

claims.title: Proposed family: F06, block-list counters
claims.text: The description grows slowly: 20 to 27 level-2 tokens at every record from 2.6·108 to 1.7·1010 steps, and 11 to 45 runs in the macro simulator (blocks of 4 cells) at the sampled records up to 1017 steps. The machine shares its table with 1RB1RF_1LC0LB_1RE0LD_1LB0RF_0RA0RC_1RE--- (states renamed, some of the four mirrored; related.json), started in another state. On the screen the four runs show the same list of blocks at the same moments. For example near step 6.4·107 all four tapes read blocks of 3, 1,546, 39, 1,753, 117, 1,467 and 997 pairs 01 and then a last block, of 4,405 pairs in 1RB1RF_1LC0LB… and of 4,409 pairs here. The four last blocks differ by 2, 4 and 6 pairs and the records come at slightly different steps. This is an observation at the sampled records: it is not a proof that the runs correspond, and nothing about halting is carried over. For 1RB1RF_1LC0LB… the right end is proved in Lean to be a base-3 counter on the separators of such a list (bb6-1RB1RF_1LC0LB/lean/Counter.lean). Those theorems are about that machine's table with its own state names; they apply here only after the renaming is carried through, which has not been done. A list of blocks with a base-3 counter is F06.

claims.title: The four machines would halt together if the first run never gets short
claims.text: From the Lean theorems, the four runs stay shifted copies, and the four machines halt together or not at all, provided the first run of the run of 40600 has at least 3 cells every time the head enters it. That is observed (at least 5 cells at each of the 57,701 entries in the first 2·10<sup>10</sup> steps, and growing) but not proved: a bounce removes 1 or 2 cells and nothing local bounds the number of bounces between two sweeps. So halting together is not established.
claims.where: README, section “One run for four machines”; holdouts/1RB0RA_1LC0RE_0LD0LB_1LA1LF_1RA0LF_1LC---/py/entries.py

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The ordinary ticks of the two common families are proved for every length. Still missing: the other tick patterns (166 of the 30,932 ticks of the first 1010 steps, besides the 238 rebuilds), rules for the left-end rebuilds, and an invariant of the block lists, kept by all rules, that keeps B off 0 1 1. A rebuild reads its blocks cell by cell. It also comes back to the right in a state that depends on the blocks there, so it does not split into the pass pieces of the ordinary ticks. A general rebuild rule would have to follow the counter it runs on the block after the turning point.

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same table as 1RB0RA_1LC0RE_0LD0LB_1LA1LF_1RA0LF_1LC--- up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each. The same table as 1RB1RF_1LC0LB_1RE0LD_1LB0RF_0RA0RC_1RE--- up to renaming, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each. The same table as 1RB0LF_1RC0RB_1LD0RA_0LE0LC_1LB1LF_1LD--- up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows yet. This machine keeps an alternating tape cut into blocks, and its separators count like an odometer whose rules depend on the parities of the blocks. This page runs it in your browser and shows the counter.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 76,681 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).

sections.heading: Blocks, separators and complementing sweeps
html: Stop the simulator whenever the head turns at the right end. The tape is always an alternating pattern cut into blocks by single extra cells. Writing a for 10, at step 2,614 it reads
a3 1 a3 1 a12 1 a15 1 a27 A>1 1

Each sweep complements the cells it crosses, which on an alternating stretch is the same as shifting it by one cell. Moving left, A, E and D take four cells at a time (sweep_left); moving right, B and A take two (sweep_right). A separator is where two equal cells sit side by side, and that is where the head changes phase or turns. Below a list such as 3|3|12|15|27 means block lengths 3, 3, 12, 15, 27 with separators 1 (|) or 0 (.) between them.

sections.heading: An odometer read through parities
html: Consecutive right-end turns after step 2,614:
Each line is one tick. The sweep from the right passes some separators and turns at one; the rules found by running the machine symbolically, with the block lengths as variables (e even, o odd):

x | e                  →  x . e+2                    (tick_last)
x | o | o'             →  x . o+1 | o'+1             (tick_oo)
x | e . e . e          →  x . e | e+1 | e+1
x | o | o' . e . e     →  x . o+1 | o'-1 | e+1 | e+1
x | e . e . e . e . e  →  x . e | e+1 | e-1 | e+1 | e+1

The separator 1 where the sweep turns becomes 0, the 0s after it become 1s, and the blocks after it change by +1, −1, …, +1, +1. These two families cover 30,528 of the 30,932 ticks of the first 1010 steps; Lean proves the first two lines for all lengths. For example the tick from 2,792 to 2,912 is tick_last with e = 28: …16 | 28 becomes …16 . 30.

sections.heading: Rebuilds that recur
html: 238 ticks reach the left end. The head then works there for a long time and rebuilds the front of the list. The striking thing is that the same rebuilds come back, later and with more blocks behind them:

So the list behaves like a counter whose digits are themselves counters, recurring on growing scales; the list has only 14 blocks after 1010 steps, but some of them are tens of thousands of cells long.

The only halt is B>0 1 1 two steps ahead (halt_route): B on the last 0 of a block followed by a separator 1. The open steps are the tick families for chains of any length, the rules of the rebuilds, and an invariant of the lists that rules this out.

sections.heading: Four machines, one run
html: Four of the open machines have the same table once the states are renamed and, for two of them, the tape is mirrored. They only start in different states. This machine is number 103746.

idstart state (in the names of 32883)mirroredfirst run of the tape
32883Anor + 4
40600Dyesr
103746Byesr + 8
131976Enor + 12

A trip starts when the head steps onto a new cell at the end of the tape where the counter has its lowest digit. Compared trip by trip, the four tapes are the same list of runs of alternating cells, except that the first run differs by a constant: 4, 8 or 12 cells. This was checked for every one of the first 527,004 trips, up to 2·1012 steps, without a mismatch.

Why would four machines agree like this? The head can only notice the length of the first run by entering it, and there are ten ways to enter: five states, on a 0 or a 1. A Lean proof covers all ten: with 4 more cells in the run the head comes out in the same state and leaves the same cells behind. So the four runs stay copies of each other, and the four machines halt together or not at all, as long as the first run of the shortest tape never has fewer than 3 cells when the head enters it.

That last condition is the one thing not proved. In the first 2·1010 steps the run has at least 5 cells at each of 57,701 entries, and it keeps growing, but a proof needs the full theory of this machine’s rare long trips. Until then, “they halt together” is a well-supported conjecture, not a result.

sections.heading: Which family it belongs to
html: The 22 machines of family F09 (“bouncers over lists of counters, not yet classified”) were screened in one way. The machine runs from blank tape for 2·1010 steps; each time the tape reaches a new cell after a threshold, the tape is compressed twice: first repeats of one word, then repeats of groups of words. If the tape is a few growing blocks and a bounded rest, the number of level-2 tokens stays bounded while the tape grows. Everything in this section is observed in one run. None of it is proved.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.389). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.554).
After 109 steps the tape spans 76,681 cells (15,535 left of the start, 39,631 right), with a density of 1s of 0.5.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machines below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in any of the others, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

  • 1RB0RA_1LC0RE_0LD0LB_1LA1LF_1RA0LF_1LC---: rename A→B, B→C, C→D, D→A, E→E, F→F and exchange left and right; it is this table started in state D, in a mirror
  • 1RB1RF_1LC0LB_1RE0LD_1LB0RF_0RA0RC_1RE---: rename A→C, B→E, C→A, D→B, E→D, F→F; it is this table started in state C
  • 1RB0LF_1RC0RB_1LD0RA_0LE0LC_1LB1LF_1LD---: rename A→C, B→D, C→E, D→B, E→A, F→F and exchange left and right; it is this table started in state E, in a mirror

family: odometer on separators of (10)-blocks, recurring on growing scales
summary: An alternating tape cut into blocks by single separator cells. Each round trip from the right end is a tick that flips separators by a few rules depending on the parities of the blocks, like an odometer; now and then a tick reaches the left end and rebuilds the front of the list, and the whole pattern recurs on larger scales. Open.
